open_points.subject: A3 INV-014
open_points.text: INV-014: a focused test at `authenticate_staff` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which statuses and observations must the test cover to prove that authentication succeeds only for `active` and refuses `pending_verification`, `suspended`, and `disabled` without changes?
options: Test every non-active StaffStatus and one active control
Test only pending_verification because it is named explicitly
Choose one arbitrary non-active status
open_points.default_guess: Test every non-active StaffStatus plus an active control.

open_points.subject: A4 INV-001
open_points.text: INV-001: a focused test at `_authorize_project_operation` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What cases must demonstrate every guard step, the stated precedence, first-failure-wins behavior, and absence of writes?
options: One case for each guard failure plus combinations proving precedence
One arbitrary authorization failure
Only the successful sequence
open_points.default_guess: Test each step separately and pairwise combinations that prove the declared order.

open_points.subject: A4 INV-004
open_points.text: INV-004: a focused test at `conceal_authentication_failure` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which authentication flows, existence variants, responses, and project-data observations must be compared to prove concealment?
options: Compare existing and nonexistent staff/viewer identities across all authentication failures and verify identical public responses with no project data
Test one nonexistent staff email
Inspect only the exception type
open_points.default_guess: Compare matched existing/nonexistent cases for staff login and viewer entry and assert identical public disclosures.

open_points.subject: A4 INV-017
open_points.text: INV-017: a focused test at `_require_staff_scope` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What must be shown for duplicate assignments, revocation taking effect on the next check, operator scope, and administrator area-derived scope?
options: Exercise active, absent and revoked operator assignments plus administrators with absent/active/revoked assignments
Test only a revoked operator assignment
Test only duplicate assignment persistence
open_points.default_guess: Cover operator assignment states and prove administrator access is independent of assignments.

open_points.subject: A4 PLAT-REG-003
open_points.text: PLAT-REG-003: a focused test at `_authorize_project_operation` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which Registry answers must the test use to prove that a linked mutation requires server-side typed validation of the same UUID as active?
options: Cover matching active, matching archived, absent, mismatched UUID, malformed answer and Registry failure
Cover only archived status
Cover only a mismatched UUID
open_points.default_guess: Cover every non-admitting validation class and one matching-active control.

open_points.subject: A5 PLAT-REG-006
open_points.text: PLAT-REG-006: a focused test at `get_project_context` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What must the test show about live fetching, absence of persisted Registry truth, archived readability, and refusal of mutations?
options: Change Registry answers between calls and prove each read uses the new answer, stores no snapshot, permits archived reads and refuses archived mutations
Test only that get_project_context calls the gateway
Test only an archived read
open_points.default_guess: Use changing live answers and inspect persistence as well as archived read/mutation behavior.

open_points.subject: A8 INV-009
open_points.text: INV-009: a focused test at `PortalTransaction.commit` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which viewer and producer grant histories must show the uniqueness invariant and the unchanged state after refusal?
options: Attempt duplicate active grants for both viewer/project and service-principal/project pairs and verify atomic refusal
Test one viewer duplicate only
Rely only on a database uniqueness declaration
open_points.default_guess: Test both grant kinds with committed-state comparisons before and after refusal.

open_points.subject: A8 INV-030
open_points.text: INV-030: a focused test at `create_expense_from_recognition` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What must be shown for first creation, equal-fingerprint replay, different-fingerprint conflict, the single document, and complete absence of changes on conflict?
options: Test all three histories and compare Expense, ExpenseDocument and allocations
Test only a duplicate recognized_document_id
Test only equal replay
open_points.default_guess: Test creation, equal replay and conflicting replay over the complete aggregate.

open_points.subject: A8 INV-042
open_points.text: INV-042: a focused test at `register_work_payment` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What observations prove equal replay, conflicting replay, absence of factura/accounting output, and derivation of payment totals?
options: Test equal and unequal replay and inspect payment storage, accounting surfaces and recomputed totals
Test only duplicate payment_id
Test only the returned WorkPayment
open_points.default_guess: Test both replay outcomes and verify no accounting record exists and totals derive from stored payments.

open_points.subject: A8 INV-043
open_points.text: INV-043: a focused test at `publish_progress_photo` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What must show intake-id idempotency, conflict behavior, chronological gallery order, and that visibility changes leave financial and progress data unchanged?
options: Exercise equal/conflicting publication, gallery ordering and a visibility update with before/after financial and progress state
Test only duplicate intake_id
Test only photo publication
open_points.default_guess: Cover every clause of INV-043 with before/after state comparisons.

open_points.subject: A10 INV-015
open_points.text: INV-015: a focused test at `perform_recovery_override` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What must demonstrate atomic email replacement, exactly one distinct audit action, canonical account entity_id, acting administrator provenance, and absence of both email values from audit?
options: Assert all listed fields and atomic rollback on audit or account failure
Test only that an audit row exists
Test only that the email changes
open_points.default_guess: Assert the complete account-and-audit transaction and both failure directions.

open_points.subject: A12 INV-029
open_points.text: INV-029: a focused test at `authorize_snapshot_import` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which scope modes, grant states, Registry states, capability failures, concealment behavior, and ordering before content validation must be shown?
options: Cover both scope modes, absent/inactive/active grants, Registry states, capability denial and malformed content to prove authorization wins first
Test only an absent grant
Test only all_projects success
open_points.default_guess: Exercise the full authorization matrix and prove no content validation or write occurs after an access failure.

open_points.subject: A13 audit occurrence semantics
open_points.text: One audit record per action occurrence; `staff.recovery_override` carries enhanced detail via its entity reference: its record is the distinct action `staff.recovery_override` naming the account (`entity_id` = its `staff_id`) and the acting administrator; neither the replaced nor the replacement email is kept in any record, and the account's current email is the only evidence of the change (Factory code `application/staff_identity.py` `perform_recovery_override`; Owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated.)
open_points.question: Does a refused occurrence of a catalog action write exactly one rejected audit record, or do refused operations other than snapshot import and failed login write no record?
options: Every catalog action occurrence, including a refusal, writes one record
Only successful operations plus the two named rejected writers write records
A refused operation is not an action occurrence
open_points.default_guess: Treat only successful operations and the two explicitly named rejected writers as auditable occurrences.

witness.initial: An active project, authorized staff actor, and an existing expense are present.
events: The staff actor requests `expense.correct` with invalid allocation instructions.
The correction is refused before commit.
outcomes: The sentence “One audit record per action occurrence” requires one rejected `expense.correct` AuditRecord.
The later rule “Every other refused operation rolls its transaction back and writes no record” requires no AuditRecord.
witness.observer: An auditor reading the audit log

open_points.subject: A13 INV-051
open_points.text: INV-051: a focused test at `append_audit` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What must prove exactly one record for every applicable catalog action, actor provenance for every actor kind, and mandatory service key_version?
options: A catalog-wide matrix covering actor kinds, exact cardinality and service key_version
One representative append_audit call
Only validation of an unknown action
open_points.default_guess: Use a table-driven test over the full catalog and all permitted actor forms.

open_points.subject: A13 INV-053
open_points.text: INV-053: a focused test at `append_audit` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which result, significance, and reason_code combinations must be accepted or refused, and how is closure of reason codes demonstrated?
options: Test the complete result × significance × reason presence matrix and every allowed closed reason
Test only a rejected significant mutation without a reason
Test one accepted record
open_points.default_guess: Test the full combination matrix and reject values outside the closed reason catalog.

open_points.subject: A17 INV-003
open_points.text: INV-003: a focused test at `issue_verification_secret` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: How can a test at only `issue_verification_secret` prove the invariant for passwords, staff sessions, viewer tokens, service credentials, persistence, and logs?
options: Require tests at every issuing/accepting flow plus repository and log inspection
Treat issue_verification_secret as sufficient for every secret type
Test only the returned hash
open_points.default_guess: Add flow-specific persistence and log-sink tests for every secret class.

open_points.subject: A22 TXN-002
open_points.text:
TXN-001, TXN-002: the transaction guard check
  [witness: verification:transaction_guard_client_portal].
open_points.question: What failure history must the check exercise to prove that a domain error is re-raised unchanged even if rollback itself raises a persistence error?
options: Raise a sentinel domain exception and make rollback fail, then require the identical sentinel exception at the caller
Test only a successful rollback
Permit the rollback exception to replace the domain exception
open_points.default_guess: Require object-identity preservation of the original exception while suppressing or otherwise preventing rollback failure from masking it.

open_points.subject: A23 audit entity invariant
open_points.text:
A writer test that rejects a UUID object and a non-canonical string for
  `entity_id`, and a consumer test per audited mutation that reads the record
  back.
open_points.question: What must each consumer test compare to prove that the id belongs to the actually audited entity, and when must entity_id be absent?
options: Compare every record with the canonical id of the action-specific entity and test absence only for entity kinds with no own id
Only check that entity_id is a string
Only check UUID formatting
open_points.default_guess: Define the expected entity kind/id pair for every audited mutation and test the no-identifier exception explicitly.

open_points.subject: A24 immutability invariant
open_points.text:
A test per revocation cascade that the read record is untouched and the
  replacement carries the change.
open_points.question: How do revocation-cascade tests prove the broader invariant that every repository-read value remains unchanged after any use case that reads it?
options: Require mutation-sentinel tests for every use case that reads and replaces records
Limit the invariant to revocation cascades
Assume frozen model configuration alone proves all consumers
open_points.default_guess: Test every replacement-producing use case and separately verify the emitted models are frozen.

open_points.subject: A25 TRN-001, TRN-002 and TRN-003
open_points.text:
Factory focused checks `client_portal_transport_guard`,
  `client_portal_api_transport_check` and `runtime_settings_client_portal`
  (`babd5e52`, `3080ef0d`, `dc351917`).
open_points.question: What exact requests, responses, handler observations, session state, and log contents must these checks show for the three transport invariants?
options: Specify cases for untrusted hosts, oversized bodies, foreign sign-out origins, missing viewer cookies, and every redacted secret source
Rely on the check names alone
Test one representative rejected request
open_points.default_guess: Give each invariant an explicit request matrix and observable assertions.

open_points.subject: A26 exception payload invariant
open_points.text: A snapshot import test per `ImportRejectReason` value.
open_points.question: How must the tests vary exception message text to prove that the recorded reason comes from the `reason` field rather than the message?
options: For every reason, use misleading or changing message text and assert the recorded field reason
Test each reason with a matching message
Inspect only the raised exception
open_points.default_guess: Use deliberately non-corresponding messages and assert classification solely from the field.

open_points.subject: A27 deterministic ordering invariant
open_points.text: A derived-view test with two records of equal date per list.
open_points.question: How does this test prove every secondary and final id tie-breaker and stability across different repository input orders?
options: For each list, cover equal primary dates with differing times, equal dates and times with differing ids, and shuffled input orders
Use only two records with equal primary date
Assume the implementation's sort is stable
open_points.default_guess: Test each ordering key independently and repeat with shuffled and reversed upstream sequences.

open_points.subject: A28 source-supplied instant representation
open_points.text:
Times a
source supplies — `approved_at`, `published_at` of a snapshot, `confirmed_at`
of a recognition, `photo_date`, a service credential's `expires_at` — are
kept as supplied: the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC like every
persisted timestamp, never replaced by the clock (State 1 Modeling
conventions).
open_points.question: Which input datetime representations are accepted, and does “kept as supplied” mean preserve fields verbatim or preserve the represented instant by converting to UTC and dropping the offset?
options: Accept offset-aware values, convert the same instant to UTC, then remove tzinfo; reject naive source values
Treat every naive value as already UTC and normalize aware values
Store the supplied wall-clock fields unchanged regardless of offset
open_points.default_guess: Require an offset-aware source value, convert its instant to UTC, drop tzinfo, and reject naive input.

events: The portal persists the accepted snapshot.
outcomes: Preserve the supplied fields: store offset-naive `2026-11-09 12:00:00`.
witness.observer: A later reader comparing approved_at with other persisted UTC instants

open_points.subject: A30 binary_storage_root startup validation
open_points.text:
the storage
  root `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` likewise into `binary_storage_root`.
open_points.question: Is `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` required, and exactly which empty, whitespace, relative, nonexistent, non-directory, unreadable, or unsafe path values stop startup?
options: Require a non-empty absolute usable directory below the permitted storage boundary
Require only a non-empty string and defer path failure to reads
Allow a missing value and choose a default root
open_points.default_guess: Require a non-empty absolute directory path at startup and refuse unusable paths.

witness.initial: The environment has every required row and `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` is whitespace only.
outcomes: Startup refuses the invalid required storage root before serving requests.
Startup succeeds because no validation for the row is stated; the first binary read fails later.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and the first binary client

open_points.subject: A30 binary read-bound value path
open_points.text:
the binary read bound
  (`BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES`).
open_points.question: Does CFG-001 require consumers to use the `binary_max_read_bytes` RuntimeSettings field, or does the environment-variable name authorize a direct environment read despite the Classification principles and Consequence?
options: Use only `RuntimeSettings.binary_max_read_bytes`; `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` merely names its environment row
Read `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` directly at each binary read
Either source is conforming if values match
open_points.default_guess: Use only the RuntimeSettings field and rewrite the invariant to name that field.
